newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Gaelic games showcase-Cork vs Kerry football final.
newsitem.headline: Gaelic games showcase-Cork vs Kerry football final.

text.p: The gaelic footballers of Cork and Kerry will contest a national football league final that none of them really want to be involved in when they meet in the 1997 decider at Pairc Ui Chaoimh, Cork, on Sunday.
"We would have preferred to play anyone but Cork in this league final," Kerry centre-forward Liam Hassett said.
"The way it is with Cork, they are a neighbouring county and there is always fierce pressure when we play them," he added.
Cork and Kerry, two of gaelic footballs fiercest rivals for over a century, are expected to meet again in the Munster football championship final in Killarney, Kerry, in July.

Before that Cork will travel to meet Clare in the first of the Munster semi-finals in Ennis on June 22 while Kerry will meet one of three counties, Limerick, Tipperary or Waterford, in the other semi-final on June 29.
Cork only beat Clare after a replay last year before they went out of the championship to Kerry who in turn lost to Mayo in the All-Ireland championship semi-finals.
"A lot can happen between now and June. We have a very difficult game against Clare in the championship and we are certainly not looking beyond that," Cork trainer Larry Tompkins said.
Tompkins won All-Ireland winners medals with Cork in 1989 and again in 1990 and he also won a national league winners medal with the county in 1989.
Cork will field the same 15 as that which defeated Kildare 2-10 to 1-9 in the national league semi-final at Croke Park, Dublin, two weeks ago in Sunday's final.
Damien O'Neill retains his place in midfield at the expense of Liam Honohan who missed the semi-final through injury.
O'Neill will be partnered in the centre of the park by Martin Cronin who has operated as a third midfielder on a number of occasions during the league competition.

Cork have played with just four players up front and tended to crowd out midfield in many of their league outings to date and it will be interesting to see whether they employ this tactic again on Sunday.
The Cork full-forward line trio of Colin Corkery, Stephen O'Brien and Aidan Dorgan shared 2-6 between them against Kildare.

Kerry, who accounted for Laois on a scoreline of 2-13 to 1-10 in their semi-final, welcome back defender Eamonn Breen and forward Dara O'Cinneide at left-half back and right corner forward respectively.
The two players to lose out are defender Morgan O'Shea and forward Ruairi O'Rahilly.
Defender Seamus Moynihan and midfielder William Kirby have both recovered from slight injuries and they have been passed fit to retain their places on the team.
Kerry are trained by Pauidi O'Shea who won a record-equalling eight All-Ireland winners' medals and four national league winners' medals during his playing career.
Maurice Fitzgerald, 26, is Kerry's ace forward and he scored 2-5 against Laois in the league semi-final as well as creating many openings for his team-mates.
Kerry tend to start matches well -- they were 1-5 to 0-1 up against Laois after a mere 12 minutes.

CORK: Kevin O'Dwyer; Ronan McCarthy, Mark O'Connor, Eoin Sexton; Sean Og O'hAilpin, Niall Cahalane, Michael O'Donovan; Martin Cronin, Damien O'Neill; Ollie O'Sullivan, Ciaran O'Sullivan, Brian Corcoran; Colin Corkery, Stephen O'Brien, Aidan Dorgan.

KERRY: Declan O'Keefe; Mike Hassett, Barry O'Shea, Killian Burns; Seamus Moynihan, Liam Flaherty, Eamonn Breen; Dara O'Se, William Kirby; Pa Laide, Liam Hassett, Denis O'Dwyer; Dara O'Cinneide, Brian Clarke, Maurice Fitzgerald.
